posts.title_en: Municipality of Liperi Announces Scale42 Data Centre Development Project in Finland
posts.title_no: Liperi kommune kunngjør Scale42s datasenterprosjekt i Finland
posts.excerpt_en: Scale42 announces the development of a new data centre in Lipiri, Finland
posts.subtitle: Municipal cooperation supports the planned development of next-generation AI infrastructure and data centre capacity in Eastern Finland.
posts.body_html:
The Municipality of Liperi has been negotiating the leasing and sale of approximately nine hectares of land located in the new Välikangas industrial area for data centre operations. The site has attracted interest from the Norwegian-British data centre operator Scale42. The matter will be discussed at the Liperi municipal board meeting on 18/05/2026 and at the council meeting on 25/05/2026.

The data centre developer and operator intends to lease the land to carry out the necessary surveys for the construction of the data centre. Scale42 has the right to purchase the leased area at any time during the lease period, in accordance with a preliminary agreement enabling the purchase.

Construction of the data centre is planned to begin at the earliest in the beginning of 2027. The first phase of the project is expected to have a capacity of 60 megawatts. Based on commonly used estimates, data centres generate approximately 0.5–1 direct jobs per megawatt, which would mean around 30–60 direct jobs during the first phase. The total investment value of the project is estimated at approximately 800 million euros.

“We are happy to see that the new Välikangas industrial area has attracted the interest of international operators. The area is easy to build on and access, and it is located next to a power line. A data centre is ideally suited to this industrial area, and the site also offers good conditions for the project’s possible expansion, including the distribution of waste heat, creating further opportunities for local businesses and projects. This is an economically significant project and precisely the kind of development project that was sought when zoning the new industrial area”, says Pellervo Hämäläinen, Liperi’s municipal manager.

Hämäläinen believes that, when realised, the data centre will also bring new opportunities for the businesses located in the area.

“Scale42 is excited to be developing a new data centre project in Liperi. The Välikangas industrial area is an exceptional location that strengthens our growing presence in Eastern Finland alongside our project in Kitee. From the outset, Liperi’s municipal leadership and local stakeholders have shown a strong commitment to enabling sustainable digital infrastructure and long-term regional growth. Their support has been instrumental in advancing the project at pace.
This development is an opportunity to create skilled local jobs, provide heat reuse opportunities, and establish long-term high-value, export-orientated operations in the region. Scale42 is committed to delivering the project responsibly, efficiently, and in close partnership with the local community, and we look forward to bringing the project into operation as quickly as possible,” confirms William Tasney, CEO of Scale42.

A data centre is a large computer that stores, processes, and transmits information, forming the back-bone of the digital economy. Practically all web-based services we use rely on data centres, and it is expected that Scale42 will deploy infrastructure to house AI technology.

posts.body_html:
Finnish Media Reports on Scale42’s Planned AI Data Centre Development in Kristinestad

Finnish regional media outlets Sydin and Vasabladet recently reported on Scale42’s planned AI data centre development project in Kristinestad, Finland, following public presentations and meetings held in the city earlier this month.

According to the reporting, Scale42 has signed a pre-reservation agreement covering approximately 126 hectares of land on the eastern side of Kristinestad for the proposed development.

The project is initially planned at around 60MW of capacity, with the potential to scale to 500MW in later phases. Reporting also noted that the broader development plans could ultimately support significantly larger capacity over time as demand for AI infrastructure continues to increase.

The planned campus could include between 75,000 and 250,000 square metres of building area, with construction potentially beginning from 2027 onwards, subject to permitting and planning approvals.

Focus on AI Infrastructure Growth

Both publications highlighted the rapidly growing demand for AI-related computing infrastructure and the increasing scale of modern data centre developments.

Speaking during presentations covered by local media, Scale42 founder William Tasney commented on the rapid change taking place within the sector:

“Previously data centres were needed to run, for example, Netflix and Facebook. Now it is about AI, which requires significantly more capacity and therefore the facilities are also growing.”

The reporting also noted that Finland and the wider Nordic region are attracting increasing interest for data centre development due to access to renewable electricity, cooler climate conditions and available land suitable for large-scale infrastructure projects.

Employment and Regional Development

Local reporting focused significantly on the potential regional impact of the project.
Scale42 stated that the number of operational roles at the Kristinestad facility would depend on the final scale of deployment and customer requirements, with estimates ranging from approximately 125 to 500 direct jobs, alongside indirect employment during construction and operation.
In comments reported by the Finnish press, Tasney also spoke about the importance of regional development and creating opportunities in smaller communities:
“I myself grew up in a small town where it was difficult to find work after my studies, just like in Kristinestad. Now opportunities are being created to find work and be able to stay in this beautiful place, so at the same time it's about a social ambition.”

Environmental and Community Themes

The articles also covered discussions around energy use and environmental considerations linked to large-scale AI infrastructure.
According to the reporting, Scale42 is exploring potential opportunities for reusing waste heat generated by the facility, including possible applications connected to district heating, fish farming, greenhouse projects and other local initiatives.
The proposed design approach described in the reporting includes low-rise buildings integrated into the surrounding landscape, with woodland screening and natural facade materials intended to help blend the development into the local environment.

Planning Process Continues

The City of Kristinestad approved the partial master plan for the wider industrial area earlier this year, while detailed planning work for the area continues.
According to the reporting, Scale42 hopes to complete permitting processes during 2027 in order to begin initial construction activity thereafter.
The Finnish media coverage reflects the increasing attention being placed on Nordic AI infrastructure development as demand for large-scale compute capacity continues to accelerate globally.

posts.title_en: Scale42 plans AI data centre in Kitee, Finland
posts.title_no: Scale42 planlegger KI-datasenter i Kitee, Finland
posts.alt: Kitee, Finland - Puhos industrial area site for the Scale42 data centre
posts.excerpt_en: Data Centre Dynamics on Scale42's 10-hectare Puhos site, with 30 MW available now.
posts.excerpt_no: Data Centre Dynamics om Scale42s 10-hektar Puhos-tomt, med 30 MW tilgjengelig nå.
posts.subtitle: 10-hectare Puhos industrial site offers 10 MW today and is scalable to 200 MW via the Fingrid national grid.
posts.tags: Kitee, Finland, North Karelia, Data Centre Dynamics
posts.source_html: As reported by Data Centre Dynamics and Business Joensuu.
posts.body_html:
Scale42 will develop a new AI-ready data centre in Kitee’s Puhos industrial area, eastern Finland. Construction is targeted for 2026, with operations beginning in 2027–28.

The City of Kitee has agreed to sign a Preliminary Real Estate Sale and Purchase Agreement with Scale42 for a 10-hectare plot in the northern part of the Puhos industrial area. The site offers 10 MW available today, with capacity scalable to 200 MW via connection to Fingrid’s national grid — one of the cleanest electricity mixes in Europe.

The project is expected to create 50–100 permanent jobs during operations, in addition to construction-phase employment. It marks the first industrial-scale data centre development in the North Karelia region.

"Kitee is a place with deep industrial roots and pride. We want to help be a part of its next chapter, diversifying into the digital economy." — William Tasney, CEO, Scale42

For Kitee, the project arrives as the municipality’s Puhos area transitions from its forest-industry heritage toward higher-value technology sectors.

"This project offers a huge boost to our region through the creation of new jobs." — Pekka Hirvonen, Mayor of Kitee

Business Joensuu, the regional development agency supporting the deal, framed it as an inflection point for the wider region.

"This project marks an exciting milestone as the first industrial-scale data centre development in the North Karelia region." — Pauliina Pikkujämsä, Director, Business Joensuu

Scale42’s selection of Kitee reflects the broader thesis behind its 1.7 GW Nordic pipeline: industrial sites with strong existing grid infrastructure, low-cost renewable electricity, and supportive local stakeholders — in regions where AI compute can be deployed responsibly and at scale.

posts.title_en: GIGA-42 signs MoU with Norðurþing for AI hyperscale campus at Bakki
posts.alt: Bakki, Húsavík - site of the GIGA-42 / Norðurþing AI hyperscale data centre
posts.excerpt_en: Non-binding framework with the Norðurþing Municipality on site allocation, zoning, permitting and infrastructure for a 50 MW first-phase campus on Iceland’s north coast.
posts.subtitle: 50 MW first phase next to Landsnet’s 220 kV transmission line and the Bakki substation; FID targeted 2026, first-phase operations 2027.
posts.source_html: Announcement: Global Interconnection Group · Euronext company news.
posts.body_html:
GIGA-42 Holdings has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Norðurþing Municipality to develop one of Iceland’s first AI-optimised hyperscale data centres at Bakki, Húsavík.

The MoU establishes a non-binding framework covering site allocation, zoning, infrastructure development, and permitting for a phased, modular campus. The target first phase is 50 MW, with the platform engineered to scale into a hyperscale build-out as anchor customer demand materialises.

Why Bakki

The site sits adjacent to Landsnet’s 220 kV transmission line and the Bakki electricity substation, with established fibre connectivity into the national backbone. Power delivery is dominated by clean geothermal generation, with co-location opportunities to recycle low-grade heat into adjacent industrial and community uses.

Timeline

  • 27 August 2025 — MoU signed with Norðurþing Municipality
  • 2026 — Target Final Investment Decision (FID)
  • 2027 — First-phase operations

Local impact

Construction is expected to support 100+ construction jobs with 50–80 permanent operational roles once the first phase is online. The project includes commitments to district heating reuse, potential co-location with aquaculture and greenhouse facilities, and vocational training programmes with local partners.

For Scale42 and GIG’s GIGA-42 joint venture, Bakki anchors the Icelandic end of a Nordic pipeline targeting low-carbon, geothermally and hydro-powered AI compute at industrial scale.
